pull.title: test: align rpcwaittimeout floor with steady_clock
pull.body:
Previously, `interface_bitcoin_cli.py` required the `-rpcwaittimeout=5` path to wait at least 5 wall-clock seconds before failing to connect. Under Docker CI load the process can return a few tens of milliseconds early (~40ms observed), so the floor assert flakes.

Fix by allowing 0.1s scheduling slack on that wait floor and reduce `-rpcwaittimeout` to `1`.

events.message: test: allow slack on rpcwaittimeout wait floor

events.body: `start_time` is taken before spawning bitcoin-cli and bitcoin-cli uses monotonic time, so the flake can only come from wall clock adjustment. Wouldn't replacing `time.time()` with `time.monotonic()` fix this without the slack?

rename.from: test: allow slack on rpcwaittimeout wait floor
rename.to: test: align rpcwaittimeout floor with steady_clock

events.body:
Good catch, not sure how I missed this. I presume I was confused by the LHS and RHS both doing addition. Maybe it would be clearer to understand and to read the assertion error message, when the LHS was `monotonic()-start_time`, so that only the duration is printed. Steps to reproduce:

```
faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.5" ./bld-cmake/test/functional/interface_bitcoin_cli.py 
```

comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -478,7 +478,8 @@ def run_test(self):
         self.stop_node(0)  # stop the node so we time out
         start_time = time.time()
         assert_raises_process_error(1, "Could not connect to the server", self.nodes[0].cli('-rpcwait', '-rpcwaittimeout=5').echo)
-        assert_greater_than_or_equal(time.time(), start_time + 5)
+        # Allow small scheduling slack. rpcwaittimeout is best effort wall clock.
+        assert_greater_than_or_equal(time.time() + 0.5, start_time + 5)
comments.body: seems fine, but the 5 can probably be reduced to `1`, to speed up the test
